title: What is known about 1RB1RA_0LC0RA_1LF0LD_1LE0RC_1LB1LD_1RB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RA_0LC0RA_1LF0LD_1LE0RC_1LB1LD_1RB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. At a left turn the tape is blocks of ones of lengths 1, 3, 5 separated by single 0s, arranged in long periodic stretches. Next to the left end a stretch (1 3 1 5 5)^n (as block lengths) grows by about one copy per left turn; it was reset to nothing at about 1.08·106 and 1.17·107 steps, and regrew to 106 copies by 2.6·107. The sweep rules are proved in Lean; the resets are not understood.
Lean proves no halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (10,000 by the kernel alone); the C simulator finds none in 10<sup>9</sup>.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 18,938 cells have been visited and 14,202 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.405). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.479).

claims.title: The sweep rules
claims.text: Shift rules of the two sweeps, for every repeat count and any tape around: A going right turns each 1101 into 1110 and each 110111 into 111011; D going left turns each 1101 into 0111, each 110111 into 011101 and each 11 into 01.

claims.title: A growing periodic stretch with resets
claims.text: Number of copies of 1 3 1 5 5 after the left end 1 4, at left turns: 16 at 1.6·105 steps, 28 at 7.0·105, none at 1.08·106, 82 at 9.1·106, none at 1.17·107, 87 at 1.8·107, 69 at 2.4·107, 106 at 2.6·107.

claims.title: The halt needs 1 C>0
claims.text: The only halting transition F1 is reached only from 1 C>0. In the first 109 steps C reads a 0 only 10,252 times; in the first 3·107 steps 1,959 of the 2,053 times are at the two ends of the tape, next to blank cells.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The rare moments when C reads a 0 away from the ends are where a halt could come from; what triggers the resets of the periodic stretch, and a closed description of the phases, are open.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.405). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.479).
After 109 steps the tape spans 18,938 cells (8,418 left of the start, 5,248 right), with a density of 1s of 0.75.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Periodic stretches that grow and reset
html: As block lengths, the left end reads 1 4 (1 3 1 5 5)^n …, n growing by about one per left turn and dropping to 0 at the resets (about 1.08·106 and 1.17·107 steps). The middle is made of long periodic stretches separated by short interfaces.

sections.heading: A rare state
html: It halts from 1 C>0. C reads a 0 only about 10,000 times in 109 steps, and in the first 3·107 steps 95% of those are at the ends of the tape, where the cell beside it is blank. The few others are where to look.

summary: Periodic regions with resets: a periodic word (1 3 1 5 5)^n grows at the left end by about one copy per left turn and is wiped out at intervals growing about tenfold, while long periodic stretches fill the middle.
family: growing periodic regions with resets (counter-like phases)

sections.heading: How it works
paragraphs: The tape is blocks of ones of lengths 1, 3 and 5, in long periodic stretches. Next to the left end a stretch of the word 1 3 1 5 5 (block lengths) grows by about one copy per left turn, until something wipes it out; then it grows again. The intervals between these resets grow roughly tenfold.
C reading a 0 with a 1 on its left would halt. C reads a 0 only about 10,000 times in 10<sup>9</sup> steps, almost always at the very ends of the tape where the next cell is blank.
